html:
The Waiwai are a Cariban people of the forests on both sides of the border between southern Guyana and northern Brazil, at the headwaters of the Essequibo River and along the Mapuera River.

They are known for their skill in weaving baskets and featherwork, and for gathering smaller groups into large villages. American missionaries settled among them in the 1950s and most became Christians. In Guyana their land is protected as the Konashen Community Owned Conservation Area. Their neighbours include the Wapishana, the Hixkaryana and the Trio.
